brief.title: Draft: Nepal tea export readiness pilot for India
proposedRecipients: National Tea and Coffee Development Board
brief.requestedDecision: Designate a technical focal point and review a small, producer-specific export-readiness evidence pack once the six research tasks are completed. No shipment, funding or outreach approval is implied.

findings.text: June Directive 02/2026 supersedes the earlier directive and corrigendum. Its SOP sets INR 2,000 plus GST per application; testing charges are separate. Domestic tea initially uses 20% risk-based testing; re-export tea has 100% FSSAI testing.
Official institutional routes exist for Nepal tea-sector support and Indian food-import clearance.
Indian tea import procedures changed during 2026. A June directive is listed after February rules and March amendments, so older checklists require reconciliation.
A July official laboratory list provides candidate testing institutions, but some validity periods have since expired and accreditation must be checked for the intended shipment.
Historical Nepal sector strategy and treaty materials provide context; current buyer demand, tariff treatment, commercial feasibility and shipment eligibility remain unverified.

proposedActions: Choose one producer group, tea grade, packaging specification and Indian destination.
Complete a dated rule comparison and official market baseline.
Verify importer, port, laboratory and certificate routes.
Compare support options against one transparent shipment cost scenario.
Review the resulting draft before any external contact.

directiveReview.title: Tea Board India Directive 02/2026: visual clause review
directiveReview.publisher: Tea Board India, Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India
directiveReview.documentDate: Printed 29/06/2026; handwritten day correction appears 30. Official listing: 30-Jun-2026.
directiveReview.method: Approved resumable curl completed; bundled pdftoppm rendered all three pages at 110 dpi; every page visually inspected. No installation needed.

clauses.summary: FSSAI tests all re-export tea; domestic testing initially risk-based at 20%.
Supersedes Directive 01/2026 and corrigendum; domestic and re-export clearance continues.
Importer needs valid Tea Board licence under TDECO 2005.
Declare arrival, warehouse, containers and separated tea, freight, insurance costs.
Application costs INR 2,000 plus GST; laboratory testing charged separately.
Re-export packaging design declares origin; submit before export, not import.
Tea Board issues portal import clearance; re-export tea receives clearance.
FSSAI samples arriving consignments for enlisted NABL-approved laboratory testing.
FSSAI-selected laboratory uploads results within five days of sample receipt.
Passing samples receive Tea Board clearance through Tea Council portal.
Tea imported for export must be exported within six months.
Instant and ready-to-drink tea are exempt from sampling.

directiveReview.quotePolicy: Concise original paraphrases only, under 200 words from this source. No verbatim excerpt or open reproduction licence claimed.
directiveReview.interpretationForPilot: Branch the research workflow by intended domestic sale versus re-export. Replace old fee and testing assumptions with the reviewed June rules, subject to a final amendment check for the shipment date.
unresolved: The date handwritten correction is visible; formal confirmation of corrected issue date remains open.
No explicit future commencement date is stated in the reviewed operative paragraph. Confirm shipment-date applicability and later amendments.
The SOP does not specify complete domestic risk-selection mechanics, border-by-border implementation, failure appeals or all FSSAI charges.
The SOP alone cannot establish customs tariff, origin eligibility, lab accreditation scope, importer approval or shipment clearance.
The five-day laboratory requirement is an official target, not verified actual turnaround.
